findings.text: MUST-FIX. effective_cap = max(cap, len(items)) removes the only bound on the comparator list at the compose_batch call site (workers.py:5656), whose caller does not chunk. pool_adapter.py:269-274 flattens every extracted batch into one list ('Flatten all batch items into a single list for pool compose') and hands it to compose_batch at pool_adapter.py:84; compose_batch performs no internal chunking. That path is sn run (cli/sn.py:2980). TRIGGERING INPUT: `sn run --source dd` with no --limit over an N-path extract, or `sn run <N paths>` - a 2,000-item list returns 2,000 comparator rows (measured on the landed function), where the base revision returned 30 for every N. The other two call sites are bounded (name-only chunks at 50, pool claims at 25) and are fine. Remedy: give the floor a ceiling that is not the batch length, or chunk at the pool_adapter flatten.

Durability. Moving the `added >= per_item_allowance` test before the append is behaviour-preserving, not functional: an inverted build with that test restored to its post-append position produces byte-identical ordered output at n=1,2,3,5,10,25,30,31,50,200 and passes all three of the node's tests. The declared 'allowance-floor' control mutates the pre-existing max(1, cap // len(items)) instead, so this third of the change has neither coverage nor a control. Either drop it from the claimed change set or pin what it is meant to protect.

Misreport. The comment above the changed call still reads 'Deduplicate across items, give each item a share, and cap at 30 total.' After this change that site returns len(items) rows whenever the batch exceeds 30, and it is the site whose caller does not chunk. An operator reading it while debugging compose prompt size is told the wrong bound.

Not a defect, worth recording. The offload's real effect is unremarked: the synchronous per-item searches previously blocked the event loop and were therefore serialised across compose workers; off-loop they run concurrently up to the compose concurrency, each opening its own short-lived GraphClient. I found no main-thread-only construct on the pure-vector path, and the only get_running_loop use (search.py:1433, _run_streams_concurrent) is not reached by it, so the offload is safe - but concurrency against the graph is a new property of this code, not a neutral move.

justifications.durability: CAN THE CHANGE BE INVERTED WITH THE SUITE STILL GREEN - YES, FOR ONE OF ITS THREE PARTS. I rebuilt the head function with the allowance test moved back to its pre-change position after the append (keeping effective_cap) and compared ordered output against head at n=1,2,3,5,10,25,30,31,50,200: it differs nowhere. Replaying the node's own three behavioural assertions against that inverted build, all three pass. The reordering is a behaviour-preserving refactor, not a functional change, and nothing pins it. The other two parts are pinned: effective_cap by the n=31/50 count assertion plus its red control, and both offloads by the AST test asserting direct_calls == [] and exactly two awaited asyncio.to_thread calls. DOES THE NEW INVARIANT HOLD AT EVERY CONSTRUCTION SITE - the floor lives inside the single function and both call sites take the cap default, so there is no second construction site to diverge. The cap <= 0 early return still bypasses the floor entirely, which is the correct explicit-disable path and no caller uses it. per_item_allowance is still derived from cap rather than effective_cap; I checked the regimes that separates (cap=100/len=200 and cap=100/len=50) and both stay consistent, so it is not a defect today. DOES ANY EXISTING TEST ASSERT THE REPLACED BEHAVIOUR - no. grep for _collect_nearby_name_comparators finds only this one test file, and its cap assertion was rewritten in the same commit from a flat 30 to max(30, item_count). No other test asserted a 30-row total. BYPASSABLE ON AN INPUT THE NODE'S TESTS DO NOT CONSTRUCT - the tests construct 25, 31 and 50 items. Nothing constructs a length the pool_adapter site can actually deliver, which is exactly the input that turns the floor into an unbounded total.
justifications.evidence: The worker's controls are real and I opened them rather than trusting the list. negative-control-effective-cap.log line 1 reads 'MUTATION: effective_cap = max(cap, len(items)) was replaced with effective_cap = cap.' and the run is FF exit 1; negative-control-allowance-floor.log line 1 reads 'MUTATION: per_item_allowance = max(1, cap // len(items)) was replaced with per_item_allowance = cap // len(items).' and is likewise red. Baseline and after suites are the same command at named revisions, both completed, and the 23 terminal ids are identical base-to-after with passes +2, so added failures 0 is supported. Scope is exactly the four declared paths (git diff --stat 3a9d055..45f1413: workers.py 20, test_comparator_budget_share.py 57, two HTML). TWO ACCURACY DEFECTS IN THE REPORT, neither of which changes the suite result. First, the manifest states 'bare allowance byte-identical at n=1,5,25,30,31,40,50,200'; that cannot be true of the landed function at n=31/40/50/200, where totals are 31/40/50/200 against the base's 30. I verified the claim that IS true - base and head produce identical ORDERED output at n=1,2,3,5,10,25,30 - so the intended statement is sound and the stated one is not. Second, the control named 'allowance-floor' mutates the pre-existing max(1, ...), not the statement reordering the report lists as one of three changes; that reordering has no control (see durability).
justifications.fit: The change reads like the module and the docstring states the mechanism and the trade rather than citing a plan. No plan labels, no ticket references, no attribution; commit subject is conventional with a body. The offload matches the file's existing idiom - compose_batch already does `await asyncio.to_thread(_enrich)` four lines above the new call. DOES THE TO_THREAD OFFLOAD CHANGE ORDERING OR EXCEPTION BEHAVIOUR CALLERS DEPENDED ON - exceptions, no: asyncio.to_thread re-raises in the awaiting coroutine, the searches are wrapped by _search_nearby_names which swallows every Exception, and the compose_worker driver at workers.py:4579 catches Exception around the call with the lease release in a finally. Cancellation, effectively no: the lease is only acquired at workers.py:3908, long after the new suspension point, so a cancellation there leaks nothing; and compose_batch already had a to_thread await ahead of this one. I checked for main-thread-only constructs on the search path (signal., get_event_loop, asyncio.run, get_running_loop, threading.main_thread across graph/client.py, embeddings/encoder.py, embeddings/config.py, standard_names/search.py) and the only hit is _run_streams_concurrent, which the pure-vector path does not reach. search_standard_names_vector opens its own short-lived GraphClient per call, so no session is shared across threads. The one real change it does introduce is unremarked: the synchronous searches previously blocked the event loop and were therefore serialised across compose workers; off-loop they now run genuinely concurrently, up to the compose concurrency. That is the point of the change, but it is worth a line in the docstring. ONE MISREPORT: the comment immediately above the changed line at workers.py:5652-5654 still reads 'Deduplicate across items, give each item a share, and cap at 30 total.' That is now false at the one call site where it matters most, and it is the first thing an operator debugging compose prompt size will read.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT: MUST-FIX. Read from the landed diff at the integrated head (git show f0a7c40b8; content re-verified at HEAD 5fbf21830 by the markers the change INTRODUCED: 5 occurrences of effective_cap and 2 of asyncio.to_thread(_collect_nearby_name_comparators, plus 0 remaining direct 'nearby = _collect_nearby_name_comparators' sites). The headline property holds and I reproduced it independently rather than reading the report: exec'ing the base-revision function (3a9d055) and the head function side by side over identical synthetic searches gives base contributors 25/30/30/30/30/30 against head 25/30/31/50/200/2000 at n=25/30/31/50/200/2000. The n=31 and n=50 defect is real and is repaired. IS THE TOTAL NOW UNBOUNDED IN ANY REGIME - YES, AT ONE OF THE TWO OFFLOADED CALL SITES. effective_cap = max(cap, len(items)) makes the returned list exactly len(items) whenever len(items) > 30, and the same probe returns 2000 comparators for a 2000-item list. That is safe only if every caller chunks. WHAT IS THE LARGEST BATCH THE CALLING CODE CAN ACTUALLY PRODUCE - the report's answer (50, from group_for_name_only) is correct for the compose_worker site at workers.py:3792 and for the loop.py pool site (claim_generate_name_batch uses DEFAULT_POOL_BATCH_SIZE = 25, graph_ops.py:15961), but it is WRONG for the second offloaded site at workers.py:5656. compose_batch does no internal chunking, and its pool_adapter caller explicitly discards the chunking: pool_adapter.py:269-274 is commented 'Flatten all batch items into a single list for pool compose' and passes that single flat list to compose_batch at pool_adapter.py:84. That path is `sn run` (cli/sn.py:2980 imports run_explicit_paths inside sn_run, registered at sn.py:1282), and _seed_explicit_paths returns one item per argv path with no chunk at all. TRIGGERING INPUT: `sn run --source dd` with no --limit, or `sn run <N paths>` with N large. Before this change the comparator block was 30 rows whatever the extract size; after it, the block is one row per extracted candidate, so a 2,000-path extract puts 2,000 comparator entries into a single compose prompt. The cap parameter no longer caps at the only call site that was never bounded by a caller. The floor is the right idea; it needs a ceiling that is not the batch length - e.g. max(cap, min(len(items), a stated maximum)) - or the pool_adapter flatten needs to chunk.

Nothing outside them. Both commits are ancestors of the integrated head 5fbf21830 and the content survived the merge, checked by the markers the change introduced rather than by reachability alone. No generated file staged, no plan-version or section-declaration mutation in the three-line plan edit.
